title: Australian Security Intelligence Organisation Amendment Bill (No. 1) 2025
short_title: Australian Security Intelligence Organisation Amendment Bill (No. 1) 2025

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would amend the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation Act 1979 to extend the compulsory questioning warrant framework of the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation (ASIO) for a further 18 months.
It would do this by changing the sunset date in section 34JF of the Act from 7 September 2025 to 7 March 2027, so Division 3 of Part III continues to have effect until then.
The bill contains a single amending item, has no financial impact, and would commence the day after the Act receives Royal Assent.
changes: Amends section 34JF of the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation Act 1979, under which Division 3 of Part III is currently due to cease on 7 September 2025.
Extends the operation of Division 3 of Part III, the compulsory questioning warrant framework, by 18 months to 7 March 2027.
Keeps in force for that period the apprehension, search and travel document provisions, offences and safeguards that sit within Division 3, without altering them.
Commences the day after the Act receives Royal Assent.
summary.affected: ASIO, the Attorney-General who issues questioning warrants, people who may become the subject of compulsory questioning warrants, including children aged 14 and over in politically motivated violence matters, and police officers exercising apprehension powers would be affected.

divisions.question: Australian Security Intelligence Organisation Amendment Bill (No. 1) 2025 - Second Reading - Agree with the bill's main idea

speeches.speaker: Tony Burke
speeches.brief: Moved the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation Amendment Bill (No. 1) 2025 to extend ASIO's compulsory questioning powers by 18 months until 7 March 2027, allowing reforms and Parliamentary Joint Committee on Intelligence and Security consideration to proceed; debate was adjourned.

speeches.speaker: Joanne Ryan
speeches.brief: Declared that, unless otherwise ordered, six bills stood referred to the Federation Chamber after debate on their second-reading motions was adjourned.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Hastie
speeches.brief: Supported the bill extending ASIO compulsory questioning warrants for 18 months to 7 March 2027. Reported that the extension would prevent disruption while substantive reforms are considered, and supported the bill without amendment while emphasising oversight, accountability and transparency.

speeches.speaker: Barnaby Joyce
speeches.brief: Supported Australian Security Intelligence Organisation amendment bills to maintain compulsory questioning powers, require post-charge questioning before a retired judge, make the framework permanent and provide Parliamentary Joint Committee on Intelligence and Security review.

speeches.speaker: Tim Ayres
speeches.brief: Moved that four bills be read a second time and had their second reading speeches incorporated. The bills would extend ASIO compulsory questioning powers by 18 months, expand Defence Housing Australia's functions, repeal pathology application fees, and establish a Pacific banking guarantee; further consideration was adjourned to the first sitting day of the next period.
